text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers. LES ECHOS
-- Prime Minister Lionel Jospin to deliver keynote policy speech to National Assembly this afternoon.
-- European partners failed to reach an agreement on a constitutional reform of European institutions in Amsterdam yesterday.

-- Lockheed Martin chairman Norman Augustine says in an interview considers alliances with Airbus partners similar to that announced yesterday with British Aerospace for the Joint Strike Fighter programme. It notably considered Aerospatiale [AERP.CN] and Thomson-CSF , provided they would be privatised.
-- Moulinex posts a 29 million franc profit for the year to March 31, its first profit in five years.
-- Rhone Poulenc considers selling three to five billion francs worth of assets in basic chemistry activities.
LA TRIBUNE
-- Merger of Suez and Lyonnaise des Eaux to be formalised today.
-- Airbus calls for a 30 to 50 percent cut in aircraft component supplier prices.
L'AGEFI
-- Bank CIC choses consumer loan firm Cetelem to manage its payment card services.
-- La Poste expects 200-billion-francs of business in life-assurance products in 1997.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- Alcatel Alsthom and Loral to form strategic alliance in multimedia satellite networks.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- Estimates for gap in social security finances ranges from 42 to 45 billion francs, compared with a 30 billion francs government forecast, due to a fall in revenue rather than a hike in spending.
-- Turnover in temporary work sector rose 13.5 percent since January.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- Shares in LVMH luxury goods group fell by 1.7 percent after it announced it had bought a 0.23 percent stake in Grand Metropolitan , on fears it could hurt return on equity.
